emergencyNumber: 112 (ambulance), 110 (police), 155 (gendarmerie in rural areas), 112 (also for emergency fire)
healthcareSystem: Universal (General Health Insurance / SGK for residents)
qualityNotes: Healthcare has improved significantly in recent years. Major cities (Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir) have excellent private hospitals with English-speaking staff. Public hospitals are adequate but often overcrowded. Medical tourism is a major industry — especially for hair transplants, cosmetic surgery, and dental work.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 9am-7pm. Each area has a rotating on-duty pharmacy (nöbetçi eczane) open 24/7. You can find the nearest 24/7 pharmacy by searching online or asking any pharmacy. Major chains like Grifin and Acibadem are common in cities.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies (eczane) are widely available. Many common medications are available OTC without prescription — this is one of the easiest countries in Europe for pharmacy access. However, for prescription medications, you'll need a Turkish doctor's prescription.
prescriptionRules: Many medications that require prescriptions elsewhere are available OTC in Turkey. For controlled substances and prescription medications, you'll need a Turkish doctor's prescription. Some medications may require a special import permit.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is a controlled substance. A prescription may be required for certain codeine products.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances requiring a Turkish prescription and special authorization from the Ministry of Health.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid pain medications (tramadol, morphine derivatives)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances. A special permit from the Turkish Ministry of Health is required.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis / CBD with THC
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis and THC products are illegal in Turkey. This includes CBD products containing any amount of THC.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Bring sufficient supply in original packaging. For any potentially controlled medications, bring documentation. Declare all medications at customs.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not legally required but strongly recommended.
travelInsurance.tips: Private hospitals in tourist areas often have direct billing agreements with international insurers. Public hospitals are less expensive but may not have English-speaking staff. Medical tourism is well-developed — even for non-tourists, private healthcare is affordable.

recommended: Typhoid (for extended stays or rural travel)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers from most countries.

waterNotes: Do not drink tap water in Turkey. Drink bottled water only. Ice in drinks at reputable restaurants is generally safe (made from purified water).
foodSafetyTips: Turkish cuisine is delicious and generally safe. Street food (döner, simit, kokoreç) is popular and safe from busy, popular vendors. Avoid raw salads in basic establishments — cooked food is safer. Watch out for meat doner kebabs that may have been sitting out. Turkish delight and sweets are generally safe.
medicalTourismNote: Turkey is one of the world's top medical tourism destinations, especially for hair transplants, cosmetic surgery, dental work, and eye surgery. Costs are 50-80% lower than in the US or UK.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Turkey. Emergency numbers (112), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccination requirements, and medical tourism guide.

hospitals.notes: Serves the Mediterranean resort coast. International department.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Turkey is a major dental tourism destination. Excellent quality at very competitive prices.
dentalCare.costRange: TRY 500-1,500 ($15-45) for consultation; dental implants from $300-600
dentalCare.notes: Istanbul and Antalya are dental tourism hubs. Prices are 60-80% lower than Europe/US. Many clinics offer package deals including hotel. Quality varies — choose JCI-accredited facilities.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Hospital emergency departments handle dental emergencies. Private dental clinics often open on weekends.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available in Istanbul through international practices and American Hospital.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services in English mainly in Istanbul. Private therapy: TRY 1,000-3,000 per session.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Turkey's accessibility is improving. Modern areas in Istanbul and resort areas are accessible. Historic sites and rural areas have significant barriers.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Istanbul Metro is accessible. Modern trams are low-floor. Accessible taxis available by request.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Hagia Sophia and Blue Mosque have wheelchair access. Grand Bazaar is very challenging. Cappadocia's landscape is not wheelchair friendly. Resort hotels in Antalya are generally accessible.

insuranceClaimProcess: Turkish hospitals experienced with international insurance. American Hospital and Acıbadem offer direct billing. Keep all fatura (invoices) and medical reports. English documentation available at international hospitals.
